series.label: GDP at PPP, constant 2021 international dollars
series.definition:
This indicator provides values for gross domestic product (GDP) expressed in constant international dollars, converted by purchasing power parities (PPPs). PPPs account for the different price levels across countries and thus PPP-based comparisons of economic output are more appropriate for comparing the output of economies and the average material well-being of their inhabitants than exchange-rate based comparisons. 

Gross domestic product is the total income earned through the production of goods and services in an economic territory during an accounting period. It can be measured in three different ways: using either the expenditure approach, the income approach, or the production approach. This indicator is expressed in constant prices, meaning the series has been adjusted to account for price changes over time. The reference year for this adjustment is 2021. The PPP conversion factor is a currency conversion factor and a spatial price deflator. PPPs convert different currencies to a common currency and, in the process of conversion, equalize their purchasing power by eliminating the differences in price levels between countries, thereby allowing volume or output comparisons of GDP and its expenditure components.
series.scope: country/economy national accounts; not a sector or shipment measure
series.estimate_label: Publisher-adjusted national-account estimates; blank native observation statuses do not identify which individual cells were estimated or extrapolated.

series.label: GDP per person at PPP, constant 2021 international dollars
series.definition:
This indicator provides values for gross domestic product (GDP) per person expressed in constant international dollars, converted by purchasing power parities (PPPs). PPPs account for the different price levels across countries and thus PPP-based comparisons of economic output are more appropriate for comparing the output of economies and the average material well-being of their inhabitants than exchange-rate based comparisons. 

Gross domestic product is the total income earned through the production of goods and services in an economic territory during an accounting period. It can be measured in three different ways: using either the expenditure approach, the income approach, or the production approach. The core indicator has been divided by the general population to achieve a per capita estimate. This indicator is expressed in constant prices, meaning the series has been adjusted to account for price changes over time. The reference year for this adjustment is 2021. The PPP conversion factor is a currency conversion factor and a spatial price deflator. PPPs convert different currencies to a common currency and, in the process of conversion, equalize their purchasing power by eliminating the differences in price levels between countries, thereby allowing volume or output comparisons of GDP and its expenditure components.
series.scope: country/economy national accounts; not a sector or shipment measure

limitations: The uniform US GDP-deflator multiplier expresses current USD amounts in a common2021US-dollar reporting unit. It does not remove country-specific inflation, exchange-rate changes or industry-specific price changes, and is not a sector-volume measure.
The US GDP price basket is a broad proxy for dollar purchasing power, not a household CPI or the sector’s own producer/input prices.

Apply the one common multiplier to monetary reporting fields only, after the unchanged currentUSDmodel solve. Do not alter modelA,L,sourcecoefficients,ratios,percentages,tonnage or emissions quantities.

PPP macro GDP and per-capita GDP are copied from their published constant2021international-dollar series, not derived locally. They are national context, not a conversion of sector accounts, trade flows, wages, company profits or scenario responses.
WDI GDP is a national market-price aggregate while ICIO value added uses source basic-price accounts. They are not forced to reconcile and sector shares against PPP GDP are not inferred.

Current World Bank source vintage is distinct from the retained OECDICIO2025 source vintage. Revisions, national-account rebasing, currency redenominations, survey benchmarks, interpolation and extrapolation can affect figures.
Native observation statuses are blank in these downloaded context rows. Source methods list official accounts and staff estimates, so unflagged values are not claimed to be direct measurements.
The raw2020–2022countrydeflator,PPPconversionfactor,currentGDP LCU andUSD downloads are retained for audit only. No localcurrency/FXbridge or sectorPPPfactor is published or applied.
ROW has no country PPPcontext; TWN has no exact matching World Bank country record. No nearest-country match, regional allocator,carryforward or imputation fills these gaps.
Missing or unavailable source cells remain null and ineligible, not zero. Historical geographic identities are not reassigned.
